title: Filtering Grouped Aggregates with HAVING
realWorldScenario: Marketing wants to identify VIP customers who have placed 2 or more orders.
questionStatement: Write a query on the `orders` table grouping by `customer_id`, returning `customer_id` and `order_count` for all customers who have placed 2 or more orders, sorted by `order_count` descending.
starterCode:
-- Customers with 2 or more orders
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY order_count DESC;
hints: Use HAVING to filter aggregated values like COUNT(*).
WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY; HAVING filters groups after.
